newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
SUGAR: World market for October 4, 1996
White sugar futures in London edged higher on light short-covering in a very thin market. December added $1.00 to close at $326.10. There was no fresh news to influence prices.

In New York raw sugar futures closed higher across the board in a thinly-traded session. March added 8 points to close at 10.93 cents/lb, while May ended 6 points higher at 10.84 cents/lb. The back months added 1 to 6 points. Given current fundamentals, chances for higher prices are slim.
FUNDAMENTALS
ALGERIA - Algeria, which is suffering from a shortage of sugar for its domestic market in the past few weeks, has bought 70,000 tonnes, official sources said.

Earlier, the country's state-owned company Entreprise Nationale du Sucre (ENASUCRE) estimated 1996 production (including the refining of imported raws) at 180,000 tonnes, white value, up from 169,130 tonnes in 1995. Production in 1997 was expected to reach 225,000 tonnes. A lack of hard currency funds has apparently delayed sugar imports.

UKRAINE - Most of Ukraine's 192 sugar factories are standing idle as a result of raw material shortages caused by lack of diesel fuel supplies to farmers, informed sources said. Only 57 factories were working, some only at 50 per cent of capacity, compared with 161 at the same time last year, it was added.

A total of 1.4 million tonnes of sugar beet has been delivered to factories by September 30, compared with 5.6 million tonnes by the same date last year. Factories so far have produced 44,000 tonnes of sugar from 523,000 tonnes of beet, against 373,000 tonnes from 3.5 million tonnes last year. The extraction rate in 1996 was 8.4 per cent, sharply down from the 1995 level of 10.6 per cent.
According to industry sources, the overall sugar beet harvest in 1996 could total 26 million tonnes, down from 30 million in 1995.

CHINA - Sugar imports in August 1996 amounted to 74,313 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from last year's 224,123 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1995/96 (September/August) up to 1.94 million tonnes against 2.91 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 1.33 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were Thailand with 628,350 tonnes raws against 1.04 million tonnes, Cuba with 449,342 tonnes against 668,621 tonnes, Australia with 351,995 tonnes compared to 618,385 tonnes and Brazil with 211,277 tonnes against 45,500 tonnes.

Sugar exports in August 1996 reached 46,009 tonnes compared to 30,006 tonnes in August 1995. This brought total exports in 1995/96 up to 830,203 tonnes against 540,004 tonnes in 1994/95 and 1.10 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Saudi-Arabia with 288,239 tonnes whites against 116,164 tonnes, Indonesia with 153,888 tonnes against nil and Hong Kong with 85,735 tonnes compared to 37,437 tonnes.

FRANCE - Sugar imports in July 1996 reached 48,904 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 54,806 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 424,825 tonnes against 310,568 tonnes. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 364,140 tonnes compared to 389,982 tonnes in 1993/94.
Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were Reunion with 156,022 tonnes raws against 137,313 tonnes and Swaziland with 53,977 tonnes compared to 50,162 tonnes.

Sugar exports in July 1996 amounted to 214,207 tonnes against 273,153 tonnes in July 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/July 1995/96 up to 2.52 million tonnes against 2.73 million tonnes in 1994/95. Total exports in 1994/95 reached 3.07 million tonnes against 2.82 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were Belgium-Luxembourg with 457,968 tonnes whites against 885,255 tonnes, Spain with 207,037 tonnes compared to 171,823 tonnes and Turkey with 200,302 tonnes compared to 81,951 tonnes.
F.O. LICHT - Our first estimate of world sugar production 1996/97 will be released later today.
TENDERS
Sri Lanka again postponed a tender for 12,500 tonnes of white refined sugar on October 4, but planned to call for fresh bids early next week, government sources said.
